thread:
maria: hey team, quick UX sync for prompt-sets regression list. users with >30 diffs report scanning fatigue. thinking about two proposals: subtle row banding + a "Compact / Comfortable" toggle, or keep single-line rows but fold tiny diffs. thoughts?

sam: banding wins for scannability. separate visual groups help eyes track across columns. avoid thick separators.

devin: compact toggle is good but default should be "Comfortable" for new users. store preference per account. add a keyboard shortcut to toggle.
jordan: copy nits: in bulk approve modal, change CTA to "Approve selected revisions" and show exact count in button. makes intent explicit.
alex: a11y: current yellow inline highlights are low-contrast in dark mode. suggest accessible shades and add a sibling icon for status. also ensure focus ring on rows is distinct from hover.
sam: behavior: when a row opens the detail panel, set focus to the panel header and trap focus inside. currently keyboard users get lost.
maria: fold tiny diffs idea: render short inline preview for 1-2 token diffs, with "Show full diff" button for details. reduces noise.
devin: metric idea: add approve_undo_rate and density_toggle_usage. helps detect accidental mass approvals or preference popularity.
aria-bot: ticket UX-701 created: "regression list density + a11y fixes" assigned @maria, labels: design, accessibility.
maria: thanks. I'll update Figma with banding + compact toggle mock and post screenshots in this thread later today. if anyone wants to pair on the prototype DM me. :sparkles:
